subject: Generate figure files but exclude from document?

messages.author: 30b406a9189eeb25
messages.subject: Generate figure files but exclude from document?
parts:
Hi list,

Is there a way to have knitr still generate figures, but not print them in the document?  If not, how about making this an option from fig.show?

The use case I imagine is the following.  I'm writing a manuscript for a journal with wonderfully archaic but common policies: they will not take pdf format (they don't say what they *will* take), they will only take eps graphics and do not want them included in the text.  With the option above, it seems like it would be easy to generate the format they require automatically when necessary (knitr + pandoc + Makefile).

(Or maybe externalization of the figures can be done with pandoc after knitr makes output markdown?)

-Carl



--
Carl Boettiger
UC Davis

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Generate figure files but exclude from document?
parts:
If you want to exclude the whole chunk output (including figures), you
can simply use include=FALSE; all results are still generated by not
included.

If you only want to exclude figures in particular, it is also easy --
reset the plot hook so that plots are not included, e.g.

knit_hooks$set(plot = function(x, options) "") # insert empty strings for plots

other types of results will remain there.

Regards,
Yihui

Any hints on getting eps instead of postscript?  Looks like this requires setting optional arguments to postscript, e.g. from the help page:

  ## for inclusion in Computer Modern TeX documents, perhaps
     postscript("cm_test.eps", width = 4.0, height = 3.0,
                horizontal = FALSE, onefile = FALSE, paper = "special",
                family = "ComputerModern", encoding = "TeXtext.enc")


Any chance tables could be created externally to? i.e. somehow have their output written to a file instead? 

-Carl

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Generate figure files but exclude from document?
parts:
Tables are a part of the text output, and you can use include=FALSE
with split=TRUE to split the chunk output into a separate tex file,
which can be included later manually by, say, \input{table1.tex}. This
should make those archaic journals happy.

Regards,
Yihui

parts:
Nice idea.  split doesn't seem to be creating external files for me though?


In chunks that have tables, I've set the chunk options as:

``` {r Table1, results="asis", include = getOption("knitr.include"), split = getOption("knitr.split")}
xtable(corr.model)
````
and I've written something like

option(knitr.include=FALSE)
option(knitr.split=TRUE)

into the compile script when doc format is requested.  This toggles include correctly, but I'm not seeing a Table1.tex file created anywhere?

 
Goodness knows what I'll do with the tex file to get the table into doc format, don't suppose pandoc will handle that. 

-Carl

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Generate figure files but exclude from document?
parts:
Oh sorry, split only works for tex and html at the moment. I have not
implemented it for markdown yet, but you are free to modify the
'chunk' hook which should be very simple, e.g.

knit_hooks$set(chunk = function(x, options) {
if (!options$split) return(x)
cat(x, file = fig_path('.md', options))
''
})

Regards,
Yihui
